speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you had an episode of loss of consciousness; to ensure your safety, can you tell me exactly what you were doing right before you passed out?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reflex Anoxic Seizure (Micturition Syncope). The rapid loss of consciousness immediately following urination in a 53-year-old male, with quick recovery and no incontinence, is classic for reflex anoxic seizure triggered by vagal stimulation during micturition. I am confident in this diagnosis based on the clinical presentation.
